messages:
Alyssa (sales): Hey team — customer (FinovateX) is asking for temporary access to our SOC 2 extracts and a signed NDA. Procurement pushed their review window by 10 days, we need an interim "bridge" or confirmation so POC can start next week. Who can help with an acknowledgement letter + redaction guidance?

Mike L (legal): We can do an interim acknowledgement, but we need a signed mutual NDA or a written acceptance of limited-scope access from FinovateX. If they can't sign quickly, I can issue a bridge-letter that says: 'Redwood will provide redacted SOC 2 extracts for evaluation only; no redistribution.' Need customer legal name + POC email.

Tariq (security): For extracts: we usually provide SOC2 sections A.2, A.3, and control narratives with sensitive fields redacted (IPs, credentials, 3rd-party contract terms). Recommend triple-level redaction: (1) redaction of creds, (2) replace internal hostnames with placeholders, (3) redact vendor contract identifiers. If customer needs deeper detail we escalate to Security review.

Eve (solutions): For the POC we can do time-limited S3 access to a prepped package. Steps: 1) signed NDA OR bridge-letter signed by our legal, 2) security acceptance email from customer POC, 3) we provide presigned URL (48h) or temp IAM creds scoped to s3://redwood-soc2/finovatex-temp/. If procurement timeframe slips, we can push access window.

Nadia (revops): FYI procurement notified us today — expected PO timeline moved from 3/22 to 4/1. Customer still wants POC next week though. If legal issues delay, can Sales accept a written risk acknowledgement from FinovateX and capture it in the deal record? I can log that in the CRM for approvals.

Mike L (legal): I can draft the bridge-letter today. Need: customer legal entity, POC email, and confirmation they won't redistribute. Draft snippet (can reuse):

```
Interim Acknowledgement:
Redwood Inference will provide limited, redacted SOC 2 report extracts for the sole purpose of evaluating Redwood's services in a non-production proof-of-concept. The recipient agrees not to redistribute, publish, or rely on these extracts for compliance assertions. This interim access does not constitute a substitute for a full SOC 2 report.
```

Tariq (security): Once Mike posts the draft, I need to approve the redaction checklist. Also, we'll attach a hash list (SHA256) for integrity, and audit access logs. No screenshots allowed per our control.

Alyssa (sales): Customer legal: FinovateX Holdings, Inc. POC: jordan@finovatex.com. They confirmed no redistribution verbally. Can we proceed with bridge-letter + 48h presigned URL?

Mike L (legal): I'll send the bridge-letter to jordan@finovatex.com for signature and copy redwood-docs-bot. If they can't sign, we accept an emailed confirmation from their in-house counsel as temporary acceptable.

redwood-docs-bot: SOC2 extracts package prepared at s3://redwood-soc2/finovatex-temp/ (redacted) — pending access grant by Security.

Tariq (security): Granting access once I sign off on the final redactions; target end-to-end turnaround ~6 hours after Mike confirms the bridge letter wording.

Eve (solutions): I'll prepare presigned URL script and a short checklist for the customer (how to download, no screenshots, contact for questions).

Alyssa (sales): Perfect — I'll update the customer and push for the quick sign. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Mike L (legal): Sending draft now. If procurement slips further, escalate to me and Nadia for exec approval.
